rows.selection_reason: No completed experiments exist, so the key uncertainty is whether a minimal RNA-only, single-profile PCA model provides a useful performance floor. This experiment tests that baseline without confounding effects from multiprofile aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image encoders, or fusion. It is the best next step because it is simple, interpretable, and establishes a reference for later comparisons of profile setting, encoder choice, and multimodal fusion.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline with moderate validation accuracy, so evidence is sparse. The key uncertainty is whether the image modality contains useful predictive signal before investing in multimodal fusion. config_010 tests an image-only ResNet50 single-profile model, keeping the design minimal and comparable to the RNA baseline. If it performs well, it supports exploring multimodal fusion; if it performs poorly, it suggests image features may not help and complexity should be added cautiously. This is the best next experiment because it isolates the effect of modality with minimal confounding changes.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile is the strongest result so far, while image-only ResNet is weak, so the RNA path is promising but we lack evidence on whether multiple profiles add value. config_002 keeps the same PCA RNA encoder and tests the minimal multiprofile extension with simple avgpool aggregation, clarifying the profile/aggregation effect before adding learned encoders or fusion. It is the best next budget use because it is directly comparable to config_001, low complexity, and reduces uncertainty about an important design choice.

The strongest result so far is RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool, which substantially outperforms RNA-only singleprofile and image-only ResNet. The key uncertainty is whether the multiprofile gain depends on the aggregation method. Testing transformer aggregation with the same RNA encoder and multiprofile setting isolates the effect of aggregation and directly extends the current best direction, making it a high-information next experiment under a limited budget.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002: 0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), clearly better than singleprofile PCA and transformer aggregation. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the RNA representation itself can improve beyond PCA under this best profile/aggregation setting. config_005 tests scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, changing only the RNA encoder relative to config_002. This is the best next use of budget because it exploits the most promising known setting while cleanly isolating the effect of RNA representation before adding image or fusion complexity.

RNA-only models dominate image-only, and the best result so far is scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool (config_005). For PCA, avgpool outperformed transformer aggregation, but it is unclear whether this holds for the stronger scvi representation. config_006 tests only aggregation while keeping the best RNA encoder and profile setting, so it isolates whether transformer aggregation can improve on the current best RNA baseline before spending budget on multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA multiprofile scvi is the strongest unimodal direction, with validation accuracy 0.653 and F1 0.628, while the only image result is a weak singleprofile ResNet50 model with accuracy 0.208 and F1 0.172. The key uncertainty is whether the image branch can be made useful by using a stronger image representation before testing fusion. config_013 tests ImageNet ViT-L in the same singleprofile, no-aggregation setting as config_010, so it isolates the effect of image encoder choice. This is the best next use of budget because it is a clean, high-information probe of the image modality: a large improvement would justify subsequent multiprofile and multimodal ViT experiments, while a similarly weak result would suggest image features are currently low-value and we should avoid premature multimodal comparisons that would confound fusion with an unvalidated image branch.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation (config_006, 0.653 accuracy / 0.628 F1), while image-only models are weak, with imagenet_vit_l slightly ahead of resnet50. The key uncertainty is whether image features provide complementary signal when fused with the best RNA representation. config_038 keeps the best RNA encoder, multiprofile setting, and transformer aggregation, and adds the stronger image encoder with simple concat fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion can improve over the RNA-only baseline. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest RNA evidence while resolving whether the image modality is worth further investment before testing more complex fusion variants.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 with multiprofile is strong for RNA-only (~0.65 accuracy), image-only is weak (~0.21-0.23), and the only multimodal result, config_038, is the best so far at 0.7207 accuracy and 0.6815 F1 using transformer aggregation and concat fusion. The key uncertainty is whether concat fusion is specifically responsible for the multimodal gain or whether weighted fusion could improve or clarify the fusion design. config_039 changes only fusion from concat to weighted while keeping the otherwise promising RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed, isolating the effect of fusion. This is the best next experiment because it is a minimal one-factor extension of the top configuration, has high expected value, and avoids changing multiple design choices under the limited budget.

The strongest completed experiments are multimodal scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with multiprofile and transformer aggregation, with weighted fusion slightly better than concat in both accuracy and F1. RNA-only scvi results suggest avgpool and transformer aggregation are close, but this has not been tested in the multimodal setting. config_037 keeps the best-known encoders, multiprofile setting, and weighted fusion while changing only aggregation from transformer to avgpool. This isolates the aggregation effect in the currently best family, has high expected performance, and clarifies whether transformer aggregation is necessary or whether a simpler avgpool configuration is sufficient before exploring new encoders or profile settings.
